overview.headline: Drag force grows with air density, speed, size and shape

keyPoints.point: Body shape and inclination effects involve viscosity and compressibility and stay complex
keyPoints.quote: In general, the dependence on body shape, inclination, air viscosity, and compressibility is very complex.

keyPoints.point: Drag scales with half the velocity squared times the reference area
keyPoints.quote: times half of the velocity V squared times the reference area A

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficient includes form plus skin friction plus wave and induced parts
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using wind tunnel testing
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyTerms.gloss: difficult value with multiple sources that sets drag level
keyTerms.quote: Determining the value of the drag coefficient is more difficult than determining the lift coefficient because of the multiple sources of drag.

keyTerms.gloss: given area chosen to characterize drag equation
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: place where coefficients are determined experimentally
keyTerms.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyTerms.gloss: form part that includes wave and induced components in drag
keyTerms.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.
